terms.meaning: a reusable building block of the React interface
one item in the Atlas, such as a role, project, or paper

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and imports
sections.what: Loads the links, router, state tools, atlas and geography data, asset path helper, motion checks, the 3D viewer, the industry artwork, and the engine type.
sections.why: The panels need each of these parts.

sections.name: KIND_LABEL
sections.title: Readable labels for node kinds
sections.what: Turns each node kind into a readable label such as Role, Build, Paper, or 3D object.
sections.why: Visitors see plain names instead of internal kind codes.
sections.watch_out: A new node kind without a label will have no name shown.

sections.name: ACTION_LABEL, byId
sections.title: Button wording and node lookup
sections.what: ACTION_LABEL maps each kind of node to the button text the visitor sees, such as Overview for a role, Read for an essay, Open project for a project and View photo for a photo. byId finds a node by its id and returns nothing when no id is given or no match exists.
sections.why: Keeping the wording in one table makes it easy to change the text for all items of one kind.
sections.watch_out: The table is typed to cover every kind of node, so adding a new kind requires adding its wording here too.

sections.name: fmt
sections.title: Coordinate format and role list
sections.what: fmt turns a number into a signed value with one decimal place and a fixed width, so coordinates line up when shown. expIds lists every role in the timeline, each with the prefix used for role ids.
sections.why: Fixed-width formatting keeps the coordinate readouts from jumping around as the numbers change. The role list sets the order used by the arrow keys and the time travel tour.

sections.name: Thumb
sections.title: Small picture with fallback label
sections.what: Thumb shows a small grayscale preview image. If there is no image or the image fails to load, it shows the item's short code in its place.
sections.why: The fallback keeps every card the same size even when an image is missing.
sections.watch_out: Once an image fails, the failed flag is never reset, so a corrected image path will not be retried until the component is recreated.

sections.name: AtlasExperience (part 1)
sections.title: Main state and the basic actions
sections.what: The main component holds what is selected, what is hovered, whether the tour is running, which panels are open and which moment is on screen. It also defines the basic actions: picking a node, clearing the selection, turning a segment filter on or off, and opening a node. Opening sends a project to its own page, a model to the 3D viewer, a role to its overview and anything else to the reader.
sections.why: Keeping the state in one place lets the top bar, bottom bar, panels and 3D engine all read the same selection.

sections.name: AtlasExperience (part 2)
sections.title: Escape steps back and the time travel tour
sections.what: back undoes the most recent open layer in a fixed order: viewer, reader, search, index, tour, selection, then segment filters. The tour effect walks through each role, lets the camera settle, plays that role's moments, pauses briefly and then moves to the next role. It ends when the list runs out or the tour is stopped.
sections.why: Likely reason: the order works like a stack, so the most recently opened layer closes first.
sections.watch_out: The order of checks in back determines what Escape closes. Reordering them changes the behavior the visitor sees.

sections.name: AtlasExperience (part 3)
sections.title: Starting and stopping the 3D engine
sections.what: On load it checks whether the browser can show WebGL. If not, it opens the index list instead. When WebGL works, it loads the engine code only when needed, creates the engine with hover, click and moment callbacks, and applies any segment or role given in the page address. When the component is removed, it disposes the engine.
sections.why: Loading the heavy code late keeps the page quick, and the index list is the fallback when 3D is unavailable.
sections.watch_out: The engine loads asynchronously, so a disposed flag prevents a late start after the component is gone. The role from the address waits 900 milliseconds, which assumes the engine is ready by then.

sections.name: AtlasExperience (part 4)
sections.title: Keyboard controls
sections.what: Escape steps back. The slash key opens search. The left and right arrow keys move to the previous or next role. These keys are ignored while the visitor types in a text input.
sections.why: Keyboard controls give a fast way to move through the timeline without the mouse.
sections.watch_out: Typing is detected only for single-line inputs. Text areas are not excluded, so typing in one can trigger the shortcuts.

sections.name: AtlasExperience (part 5)
sections.title: Top navigation bar
sections.what: Shows a breadcrumb trail with a link to the home page, the Atlas, the current role and the current item. It also shows Search and Index buttons when 3D is available and a link that exits back to the portfolio's Atlas section.
sections.why: The breadcrumb keeps the visitor oriented about where they are in the 3D view.

sections.name: AtlasExperience (part 6)
sections.title: Segment filter bar and hover preview
sections.what: Shows a row of topic buttons, with counts, that filter the 3D cloud. Shows a small preview card that follows the pointer over a node. The preview is hidden for the selected node, during the tour and on small screens.
sections.why: Filters narrow the view by topic, and the preview lets the visitor look before clicking.
sections.watch_out: The memory segment is counted by its memory flag rather than by cluster id, so it can show a different number from the other segments.

sections.name: AtlasExperience (part 7)
sections.title: Bottom controls and panel switching
sections.what: The bottom bar has previous, time travel or stop, and next role buttons, the instruction line, a camera readout and links to other sections. The panel area shows a moment card while a moment plays. Otherwise it shows the role panel or item panel for the selection, plus search, index, reader and viewer when they are open.
sections.why: Only one main panel is shown at a time, and the moment card takes priority while playback is running.

sections.name: AtlasExperience (part 8)
sections.title: Reader and model viewer
sections.what: Opens the long-text reader for an item, or the 3D model viewer for a model. In the reader, choosing a linked item opens it in 3D when 3D is on, or shows that item in the reader when it is off.
sections.why: The reader and viewer give the visitor a full view of content that does not need the 3D scene.

sections.name: HoverCard
sections.title: Preview card for hovered items
sections.what: For a role, shows its period, title, counts of engagements, builds, industries and papers, the first four engagement titles, and a hint to click. For any other item, it shows its code and type, a thumbnail, its title and a short summary.
sections.why: The card gives the visitor a preview before they commit to a click.

sections.name: MomentHud (part 1)
sections.title: Moment card during playback
sections.what: Shows a card during a moment with a counter, the company, role and period, project details or highlights, problem and geography, a row of five progress bars, and the name of the current stage. A Stop button ends playback.
sections.why: The card explains what the camera is showing as it moves through the moment.
sections.watch_out: The stage names for project scenes include one blank name, so the second stage shows no text.

sections.name: MomentHud (part 2)
sections.title: Closing the moment card
sections.what: Closes the markup of the moment card. It adds no new behavior.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: ExperiencePanel (part 1)
sections.title: Role panel header and summary
sections.what: Shows the role's title, period, job title, location and description. If there is no description it says details are to be added. It also shows the role's coordinates and, when it has any memories, a button that plays them. On phones the panel slides up from the bottom, and on larger screens it sits on the right.
sections.why: This panel is the overview a visitor sees when they step into a role.
sections.watch_out: The panel assumes the role exists and does not check for it, so an unknown role id would break it.

sections.name: ExperiencePanel (part 2)
sections.title: Project and industry lists
sections.what: Lists the role's project scenes with each project's industry, problem and places, and each item can be clicked. Then lists the industries as clickable tags. Empty lists show None recorded.
sections.why: The lists let the visitor jump straight to any project or industry from the role.
sections.watch_out: A place that is missing from the places list is dropped silently, so a typo there shows no label and no error.

sections.name: ExperiencePanel (part 3)
sections.title: Places, problems and builds lists
sections.what: Lists the role's geographies, with the first one marked base, then its problem statements, then its builds as clickable thumbnails. Empty lists show None recorded.
sections.why: These lists summarize what the role involved and link to its builds.
sections.watch_out: The base label simply means the first place in the list, so the order of the data decides which place is marked.

sections.name: ExperiencePanel (part 4)
sections.title: Moments grid in the role panel
sections.what: Shows a Moments heading with a count, then a two-column grid of photo and paper thumbnails for the selected role. Clicking a photo selects it in the 3D view, and clicking a paper opens it. When there is nothing to show, it displays an empty-state message instead.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives visitors a second way to reach each moment, from the side panel as well as from the 3D scene. The variables `photos` and `o.papers` are defined earlier in the file, which is not in this packet.
sections.watch_out: The count and the empty-state check both add photos and papers together, so changing one without the other can show a wrong count or hide the grid.

sections.name: NodePanel (part 1)
sections.title: Details panel for a selected node
sections.what: Builds the side panel for a selected item. It shows the item's code, category, title, optional image or industry art, summary, 3D position, an action button, and external links. On phones it slides up from the bottom, and on larger screens it sits on the right.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the split between phone and desktop layouts, though the responsive class names show that the layout changes by screen size.
sections.watch_out: The action button is hidden for engagement and industry items, and long link labels are replaced with the word Repository. Both rules must be kept in mind when adding a new kind of item.

sections.name: NodePanel (part 2)
sections.title: Connected items list in details
sections.what: Lists the items linked to the selected one, each with its code, title, and kind. Clicking any entry selects that item in the panel. The list is hidden when there are no links.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets visitors hop between related items without returning to the 3D view.
sections.watch_out: The list depends on the output of the neighbours function, which is not shown here, so the links can only be as correct as that function.

sections.name: SearchPanel (part 1)
sections.title: Search dialog with category filters
sections.what: Opens a search box over the scene. Visitors type a word and pick a category, and the list updates to show up to 14 matching items. Pressing Enter opens the top result.
sections.why: Likely reason: a quick way to find one item among many in a large space. The code does not state this directly.
sections.watch_out: Only the first 14 matches are shown, so a common word may hide the item you want. The results only refresh when the query or the category changes.

sections.name: SearchPanel (part 2)
sections.title: Closing the search dialog
sections.what: Closes the search overlay when the dark backdrop is clicked or the Esc button is pressed. Clicks inside the dialog do not close it.
sections.why: Clicks inside the dialog are stopped from reaching the backdrop, so the dialog stays open while the visitor types.
sections.watch_out: The stop-propagation call on the dialog is what keeps it open. Removing it would make every click inside the dialog close the search.

sections.name: IndexPanel (part 1)
sections.title: Full index of all items
sections.what: Shows every item grouped by cluster as a plain list on one page. It includes a Return to the spatial view button when a close action is supplied, and a note explaining that the 3D view is unavailable when WebGL is missing. Clicking an item selects it.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fallback for devices that cannot run WebGL, and also a readable alternative to the 3D view. The code does not state this directly.
sections.watch_out: Only items whose cluster matches one of the known clusters appear. An item with an unknown cluster is silently missing from the index.

sections.name: IndexPanel (part 2)
sections.title: End of index panel
sections.what: Only closes the index panel function. It has no behaviour of its own.
sections.why: Not applicable. This is the closing brace of the function above.

sections.name: Reader (part 1)
sections.title: Full-page reader for one item
sections.what: Opens a full-screen reading view for one item, with a sticky header and a Back to the Palace button. The title is shown, followed by an image, a video, or a memory photo with its year, depending on what the item holds. The Back button receives keyboard focus when the view opens.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives projects, papers and moments an article-style page. The focus setting probably helps keyboard and screen reader users, but the code does not say so.
sections.watch_out: Videos start playing automatically, muted and looping. A missing media path in the data will show an empty frame rather than an error.

sections.name: Reader (part 2)
sections.title: Reader body, links and related items
sections.what: Shows the body paragraphs of the item, or its summary when there is no body. Below that come external links, an Open project link for projects with a page, and a list of connected items that can be selected.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for styling only the first paragraph of a paper in a small label style. It is probably a lead line, but that is a guess.
sections.watch_out: The Open project link adds a trailing slash to the page address. Projects without a page address get no internal link at all.

summary: The side interface for the Knowledge Atlas: panels, hover card, moment display, search, index, and reader, built in React.
purpose: Shows the text, lists, and controls around the 3D Atlas scene.
why: Keeps the interface in React and the drawing in the engine.
how: Reads the atlas data and the engine, then shows panels for experience, nodes, search, and reading. Hover and selection events from the engine update the panels.
inputs: Atlas nodes, clusters, timeline, places, the engine type, and the 3D viewer and artwork components.
outputs: The panels and cards shown beside the Atlas scene.
risks: Only 2 of 28 sections were available, so most of the file is not described here.
debug: If a label is missing, check the kind lookup for that node. Other problems cannot be checked from the visible sections.
